title: Tech sucks: You have to vote with your wallet, or nothing will change
content_html:
August 09, 2026
Categories
Reading time: 4 minutes

Recently, someone on Mastodon shared this video titled "Apple Changed..." by a guy named Theo who I'd never heard of, but according to his website he's a guy who "builds things". Apps, presumably. I had nothing better to do (sleepless night...) and I enjoy a good Apple bashing, so I watched the video. In it, Theo spends an hour ranting about how terrible the experience of developing apps for the iPhone/iPad is, how Apple takes 30% of all app store and in app purchases, how awful Xcode is as a development environment and how even as a developer you have to get Apple's approval to run your own app on your own device. And how you need a second device (MacBook) to build an app for your target device (iPad) because Apple won't allow you to build the app straight on the iPad itself. And a lot more.

I'm not an iOS developer (thank god), but I'm of course aware of Apple's restrictive policies when it comes to approving and running apps on their devices, and I have no doubt that everything he says in the video is true, and that it's really an abysmal experience developing for iOS, and that as a developer (and I'd argue as an Apple user, too) you're essentially trapped in an abusive relationship from which there seems to be no escape.

But as I watched this video I kept thinking, this guy is so rightfully angry and pissed off at Apple... and yet he's sitting in front of a brand new MacBook, a brand new iPhone and a brand new iPad.

He correctly points out towards the end of the video that the only thing that matters to Tim Cook is making more money for Apple. There's literally nothing else he cares about. Not your user experience, not the environment, and also not the mental health of children and teenagers using these devices, as much as he tries to pretend that he does. The only metric that matters to Apple is "number on spreadsheet go up". And so yes, Theo might make an hour long video about everything that he thinks sucks at Apple, and he may be right about all of it.

But he still gave them thousands of Dollars.

Apple wants his money, and he gave them exactly what they wanted. The fact that he's making angry videos is simply irrelevant to Apple, because they know that when the next iPhone or MacBook is released, he'll buy that too. So why would they change anything? Because he made an angry video? They might watch it some time when they're bored and need a good laugh, but then they'll go right back to making their devices even shittier for the end user and developer. Because they can. Because people keep buying them.

Like it or not, but if being the customer of a company starts to feel more like being in an abusive relationship rather than a mutually beneficial one, it's time to think about leaving. Yes, this is scary. It's painful. It requires sacrifice. And yes I know, the ecosystem. They lure you in with the promise of "everything just works", and once you're in, you can't leave, at least not without a great deal of pain. You know what that's called btw? A trap.

Leaving sucks. But there's no other way. As long as you keep throwing money at the corporations who treat you badly, why would they change?

This train of thought is heavily influenced by a post by Dave Rupert called "Double your business with companies you like" in which he argues that even though it might not feel like it, we as consumers do have an influence over which company thrives and which doesn't, because where we spend our money influences whose sales numbers go up and whose go down. In the world of tech this is not easy of course because there are a lot of huge and shady corporations out there, and they have an enormous amount of power. But there are still alternatives.

Apple might still try to present themselves as the underdog whose products are for the people who "think different", but they're not anymore, and they haven't been for a long time. They're the evil megacorporation now, and it's time to leave them behind and go to find the real underdogs to support.

content_html_zh:
八月 09, 2026 分类 阅读时间：4 分钟

最近，Mastodon上有人分享了这段标题为“苹果改变了……”的视频 由一个名叫 Theo 的人创建，我从未听说过他，但根据他的网站，他是一个“建造东西”的人。 应用程序，大概。 我没有更好的事可做（彻夜难眠......） 我喜欢对苹果的猛烈抨击，所以我看了这个视频。 在其中，Theo 花了一个小时抱怨为 iPhone/iPad 开发应用程序的体验是多么糟糕，苹果如何占据了所有应用程序商店和应用程序购买量的 30%，Xcode 作为开发环境是多么糟糕，以及即使作为开发人员，你也必须获得苹果的批准才能在自己的设备上运行自己的应用程序。 以及您如何需要第二台设备 (MacBook) 来为您的目标设备 (iPad) 构建应用程序，因为 Apple 不允许您直接在 iPad 上构建应用程序。 还有更多。

我不是 iOS 开发人员（感谢上帝），但我当然知道 Apple 在其设备上批准和运行应用程序时的限制性政策，并且我毫不怀疑他在视频中所说的一切都是真实的，这确实是 iOS 开发的糟糕体验，并且作为开发人员（我也认为作为 Apple 用户也是如此），您本质上陷入了一种似乎无法逃脱的虐待关系中。

但当我观看这段视频时，我一直在想，这家伙对苹果如此愤怒和愤怒是理所当然的…… 但他面前却是一台全新的 MacBook、一台全新的 iPhone 和一台全新的 iPad。

他在视频结尾正确地指出，对蒂姆·库克来说唯一重要的是为苹果赚更多钱。 他确实不关心其他事情。 不是你的用户体验，不是环境，也不是使用这些设备的儿童和青少年的心理健康，尽管他试图假装自己这样做。 对苹果来说唯一重要的指标是“电子表格上的数字上升”。 所以，是的，西奥可能会制作一个长达一小时的视频，讲述他认为苹果公司糟糕的一切，而且他可能所有这些都是对的。

但他还是给了他们数千美元。

苹果想要他的钱，而他给了他们他们想要的东西。 他制作愤怒视频的事实与苹果无关，因为他们知道，当下一代 iPhone 或 MacBook 发布时，他也会购买。 那么他们为什么要改变任何事情呢？ 因为他拍了一段愤怒的视频？ 他们可能会在无聊、需要开怀大笑的时候看一下，但随后他们会立即回去让他们的设备对最终用户和开发人员来说更加糟糕。 因为他们可以。 因为人们不断购买它们。

不管你喜欢与否，但如果作为一家公司的客户开始感觉更像是一种虐待关系，而不是一种互惠互利的关系，那么是时候考虑离开了。 是的，这很可怕。 很痛苦。 它需要牺牲。 是的，我知道，生态系统。 他们用“一切正常”的承诺来引诱你，一旦你进去了，你就无法离开，至少会经历很大的痛苦。 你知道那叫什么吗？ 一个陷阱。

离开很糟糕。 但没有其他办法。 只要你继续向那些对你不好的公司扔钱，他们为什么会改变呢？

这种思路深受戴夫·鲁珀特 (Dave Rupert) 的一篇名为《与你喜欢的公司合作，让你的业务翻倍》的帖子影响，他在文中指出，尽管我们可能不这么认为，但我们作为消费者确实可以影响哪些公司蓬勃发展，哪些公司不繁荣，因为我们把钱花在哪里会影响谁的销售数字上升或下降。 在科技领域，这当然并不容易，因为那里有很多巨大而阴暗的公司，而且它们拥有巨大的权力。 但仍有其他选择。

苹果可能仍然试图将自己描绘成一个失败者，其产品是为那些“有不同想法”的人设计的，但他们已经不再是这样了，而且已经很长时间没有这样了。 他们现在是邪恶的大公司了，是时候把他们抛在身后，去寻找真正的弱者来支持了。
